picks.thesis: Convergence of two independent buyer sets. Three House members bought TSM in Jan-Feb 2026 - Gilbert Cisneros three times, including a $100,001-250,000 band on 2026-02-09, plus Julia Letlow and Richard W. Allen in $1,001-15,000 bands. Separately, TSM officers bought on the open market with no 10b5-1 plan: a broad 2026-08-07 block filed 2026-08-10 (lag 3 days) including Chairman and CEO Wei Che-Chia and a dozen VP/SVP-level filers, plus 2026-07-07 buys by Chin Yung-Pei and Hou Yung-Chin. Breadth is the signal, not size - individual insider lines run $513 to $11,143. The congressional leg is about six months stale. TSM closed 418.47, -3.6% over 30 days, between a 90-day low of 374.67 and high of 477.57.
key_risks: The congressional buys are from January and February 2026 and may no longer reflect current positioning; only the insider leg is fresh.
Insider purchase sizes are very small ($513-$11,143 per line) and may reflect routine or programmatic accumulation rather than discretionary conviction.
Disclosed congressional amounts are bands, not exact sizes, so the $100,001-250,000 Cisneros line could sit anywhere in that range.
Price is down 3.6% over 30 days and roughly 12% below the 90-day high of 477.57, so the buying has not yet been confirmed by the tape.
picks.invalidation: The August insider buying stops and reverses into Form 4 sales, or the same members file TSM sales, while price breaks below the 90-day low of 374.67.

picks.thesis: A cluster, not a convergence. Three filers bought TransDigm: April McClain Delaney repeatedly between 2026-04-15 and 2026-07-28 (mostly $1,001-15,000 bands, one $15,001-50,000 on 2026-04-16), Gilbert Cisneros on 2026-03-16, and Senator Alan Armstrong on 2026-03-27 - disclosed 116 days later. Cisneros sits on House Armed Services, which oversees the defense sector tagged here; that alignment raises the stakes and is also why such trades attract scrutiny. No Form 4 insider buying corroborates. Most of the disclosed buying is one member's steady drip in small bands, and the freshest filing carries a 6-day lag. TDG closed 1,223.48, -5.26% over 30 days, above its 90-day low of 1,148.97 and below the 1,348.49 high.
key_risks: The pattern rests overwhelmingly on one filer's repeated small purchases, which resembles a scheduled accumulation program rather than an event-driven signal.
Alan Armstrong's buy was disclosed 116 days after the transaction, so that leg is heavily decayed.
No insider Form 4 buying supports the congressional activity - the second independent signal is absent.
Bands are small ($1,001-15,000 for most lines), so the dollar conviction may be trivial.
Committee alignment cuts both ways: it is why the trades matter and why they draw scrutiny.
picks.invalidation: The recurring buyer stops filing purchases or begins filing TDG sales, or price breaks below the 90-day low of 1,148.97 with no new disclosed buying.
